title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80
config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too
config.prompt: the bare instruction 'OCR' — the model is a TRANSCRIBER

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.
6. Stop. The default extracts TEXT and makes no claim about tables, totals or entities — those are a type profile's job.
gates: A page the recogniser failed on is OMITTED and NAMED, never returned empty: an empty page is indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it, and that is how a return reconciles by losing its rows.
A document read to nothing is recorded UNREAD. It is never recorded as a document that said nothing.
on_fail: Record the document unread, with the reason and the pages, and raise it in the document reviewer. Nothing is guessed and no second reader is tried, because there is no second reader.

ocr.notes: The estate's one recogniser. There is nothing behind it.

notes: THE POINT OF A DEFAULT is that an unknown document has a stated reading. Before 2026-09-25 it had whatever the lane that happened to open it did: the party expense returns were read by a local OCR engine for a day because the lane called it directly, while the estate's chosen recogniser sat running on both boxes. title: EC party ELECTION EXPENSES return — what a party spent
applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.
5. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. A recognised reading that DISAGREES with the Commission is treated as the suspect; a text-layer or human reading that disagrees is published over the Commission (Māori Party 2020).

ocr.notes: 21 of the 40 have no text layer or print the declaration page as an image.

tables.notes: The itemised schedules behind them name the SUPPLIER on every line. That is a register this estate does not have and should; it is separate work.

title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.

A pattern that skips 'whatever is between' and then matches a number will start the number as late as it can: `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58` matched as $6.58 because the gap ate `30047`. NULL IS NOT ZERO, IN THE NOTE AS WELL AS THE FIGURE. title: EC party ELECTION EXPENSES return — what a party spent
applies_to: A registered party's return of election expenses for a general election (Electoral Act 1993 s 206I). 40 held for 2020 and 2023. NOT a donations return and never summed with one: this is money SPENT, the other is money received.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --party-expenses (the Commission's own summary page per election, captured)

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80

process: 1. Read the Commission's summary table for the election: limit, total expenses, broadcasting allocation, allocation spent, audited.
2. Take the FIRST document the table links for the party — where a return was amended the page lists the amendment first, and an amendment supersedes.
3. Read the document's text layer. If it states a total, that is the reading.
4. Otherwise recognise every page and read the same patterns over the result.

5. Take the parts from BOTH places the form prints them: `TOTAL FOR PART A` at the foot of each schedule, and the `Part A: … $x` lines in the declaration block on page 1. The schedule is preferred where both read. A return whose schedules will not recognise can still be checked against its own arithmetic this way — which is how Advance NZ 2020 was settled.
6. A person's reading, recorded in expense_readings.jsonl, outranks both.
gates: THE FORM BEATS THE AUDITOR. `Total (A + B + C)` is the party's own declaration; `Total Party Election Expenses:` is the auditor's report attached to it. TOP's amended 2023 return contradicts itself because the amendment was filed without re-issuing the report.
PART D IS NOT AN ELECTION EXPENSE. It is the broadcasting allocation spend, published in its own column. Summing every 'TOTAL FOR PART' line adds $1,248,924.19 to Labour's 2020 campaign.
A PARTIAL SET OF PARTS IS NOT A TOTAL. The form prints all three, $0.00 included, so a reading holding two has missed one.
THE FORM'S OWN ARITHMETIC. Where a reading has both a stated total and the parts, they must agree to the dollar. This is what refuses a recognised total whose characters are individually plausible.
THE LIMIT PRINTED ON THE FORM bounds the reading. Spending over it is an offence, so a figure above it is a misread or the story of the decade.
NIL IS A FIGURE (0.00); N/A IS NOT (NULL).

A PART TOTAL MAY BE PRINTED WITH NO DOLLAR SIGN. NZ Loyal 2023 prints `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58`, and a greedy gap between the label and the figure read it as $6.58 — 99.998% short, with nothing about it looking wrong. The gap is lazy AND guarded by a lookbehind; lazy alone still starts at the first digit it can reach.

THE COMMISSION'S PUBLISHED TOTAL IS A READING TOO, and it can be wrong the same way twice. Its 2020 table publishes PART A ALONE as the total for the Māori Party ($241,986.42 against a declared $301,517.96) and for Advance NZ ($364,769.96 against a declared $403,583.95). Check a published total against the form's own parts before treating the publisher as the authority.
on_fail: The Commission's published figure stands, the row records why the document could not be read, and the document goes to the reviewer. WHERE A READING DISAGREES WITH THE COMMISSION, THE COMMISSION'S FIGURE IS STILL THE ONE PUBLISHED (Arthur, 2026-09-27: "I've changed my mind. the comission should have the headline number. It should have a hyperlink to the comissions page that shows the number"), with our reading published beside it and the row tagged `spent_unreconciled` — neither is corrected to the other. This SUPERSEDES version 2, which published a text-layer or human reading over the table and a recognised reading over it where the document's own parts added to its own total (`stated_consistent`). That rule is still true about the DOCUMENTS — the Māori Party's 2020 return declares $301,517.96 against the Commission's $241,986.42, which is Part A alone — and `stated_consistent` is still read and still stated; what changed is which figure carries the headline. `query.influence.donations._spent` is the one implementation.

title: Default extraction — a document nothing recognises

ocr.notes: The estate's one recogniser. There is nothing behind it.

prompt: OCR

No second reader (card no-second-reader-qualifies-under-the-trial-s-rules). 300 dpi over 200 changed nothing measurable on 2,063 shared pages (loop pages 20 to 18, exact amounts 122 to 121 of 139 keys), so the dpi stands as written; f16 over Q8_0 agreed on every amount of the twenty-page comparison. Write-up: docs/trials/page-readers.md.
applies_to: Any document no type profile recognises. It is not a fallback in the sense of a lesser reading: it is the STATED extraction for an unknown document, so that what happens to a new file is a decision somebody can read rather than whatever the calling lane happened to do.

tooling.parse: none — the default reads TEXT, it does not claim a structure

config.pages: every page, to a cap of 80
config.cache: by document sha; a page image is immutable, so its reading is too
config.prompt: the bare instruction 'OCR' — the model is a TRANSCRIBER

process: 1. Identify the document by the sha256 of its bytes, never by filename.
2. Measure its surface: pages, characters per page, producer, longest run of text-less pages. This costs no model call and is what a person needs to write the profile that would have matched.
3. Read the text layer with pdftotext -layout.
4. Recognise every page whose text layer holds under 80 characters, and splice those readings into the text layer in page order.
5. Record which pages were recognised and which could not be read.
6. Stop. The default extracts TEXT and makes no claim about tables, totals or entities — those are a type profile's job.
gates: A page the recogniser failed on is OMITTED and NAMED, never returned empty: an empty page is indistinguishable from a page with nothing on it, and that is how a return reconciles by losing its rows.
A document read to nothing is recorded UNREAD. It is never recorded as a document that said nothing.

A GAP BETWEEN A LABEL AND ITS FIGURE MUST BE LAZY AND GUARDED. A pattern that skips 'whatever is between' and then matches a number will start the number as late as it can: `TOTAL FOR PART A 300476.58` matched as $6.58 because the gap ate `30047`. Lazy alone is not enough — a lookbehind must stop the match beginning mid-number.

A PUBLISHED SUMMARY OF A DOCUMENT IS A READING, NOT THE DOCUMENT. Where a publisher states a figure the document also states, check one against the other; the Electoral Commission's 2020 expenses table is wrong about two parties in the same way, and no amount of internal consistency checking would have found it.

TWO READERS DISAGREEING IS THE CHEAPEST DEFECT DETECTOR THIS ESTATE HAS. Both of today's reader bugs — a dollar sign read as a 9, and a greedy gap eating five digits — surfaced because something else read the same page and the answers differed. Neither was visible in its own output.
on_fail: Record the document unread, with the reason and the pages, and raise it in the document reviewer. Nothing is guessed and no second reader is tried, because there is no second reader.

  1. A CONTINUATION PAGE. The schedule runs onto a sheet the reader never opens. Green 2023's is numbered 'Page: 6.1' and carries the NINE largest donations in the return ($546,222.92). NZ First 2024's says so on its own face — 'Page added at the request of the Electoral commision due to space constraints in date feild of main form'. Look for a printed page label with a decimal, and for a sheet between two consecutively numbered pages.
  2. A CONTINUATION PAGE IS NOT A SCHEDULE. NZ First 2024's inserted sheet is a DATE BREAKDOWN whose last column is 'Donor Total' — the same figure already on the main form. Read as a schedule it produces duplicate donations; the reader took four of its detail lines as the donors' amounts and lost $89,921.04.
  3. AN AUDITOR'S STAMP OVER A FIGURE. Labour 2020 row 11 is $40,020.00 printed under Grant Thornton's circular 'Marked for identification purposes', and came back as $460.00. The stamp sits bottom-right, which is the AMOUNT column of the last row on the page — so the last row of each page of a stamped return is the one to check.
  4. A TWO-COLUMN DONOR CELL. Some forms put the donor's NAME and their STREET ADDRESS in separate table columns under one 'Donor's name and street address' heading. Green 2023 does, and the reader took the address column: 49 rows reading '<a donor's street address>' where a person's name belongs. If every donor in a part looks like an address, you are one column to the right.

prompt: This is a New Zealand Electoral Commission party donations and loans return. The DECLARATION page states Parts A, C, D, F and G and a grand total. Part A itemises donations above the disclosure threshold and is the ONLY part carrying donor names; Part G is the aggregate of everything under it and Part F is donations protected from disclosure by law, so neither names anybody — money sitting only in those parts is UNATTRIBUTED, not missing. Figures are often typed with no dollar sign and no cents (15,983), and NIL is written for zero; a declared NIL is a COMPLETE return, not a missing one. The threshold printed on a line ('of more than $1,500') is the FORM'S text and never the filed amount. Three versions of the grand total exist: (A+C+D+F+G) current with B excluded, (A+C+D+E) intermediate, and (A+B+C+D+E) on the 2019 form where B is anonymous donations and IS summed. Donor schedule pages print 'TOTAL FOR PART <X>' at the foot of each part's own table, which is a check on the declaration page.
notes:
9 of the eight parties' 56 live returns are this shape. A scan that yields nothing is recorded UNPARSED and the page says so; a second-rate figure published as a party's declared total is worse than an honest gap.

A scan cannot hide a two-column donor cell or a continuation page — it hides everything equally — so the hazards below matter here most, and the reconciliation check is the only thing that will tell you.

applies_to: A registered promoter's return of election expenses — a third party, neither party nor candidate, that spent over $100,000 on election advertising (Electoral Act 1993 s 206ZC). 20 of 21 held for 2020 and 2023.

tooling.index: ops/ec_disclosures_feed.py --promoters (the Commission's expense page, which STATES each figure)

config.pages: every page, the longest held return being 8

process: The Commission's own expense page states every figure, so the document read has a gate before it is taken.
The SCHEDULE's `TOTAL FOR PART X` beats the DECLARATION block where both read: the schedule total is the figure the itemised rows add to.
Eleven of the twenty held returns have no text layer and are read by the recogniser; the reading is cached by sha256, never by filename.
gates: THE THREE HEADS OF 2020 ARE NOT ADDITIVE AND ARE NEVER SUMMED ACROSS A ROW. The form counts an advertisement that is both an election and a referendum advertisement IN FULL under each head. Family First declared $141,224.34 under Parts A, B and C and spent it once; a row sum publishes $423,673.02 that nobody spent.
PART A IS THE PUBLISHED FIGURE. It is money spent to influence a vote for a party or candidate. Referendum advertising bought a referendum result and is carried beside it, never inside it.
2023 RAN NO REFERENDUM, so its Parts B and C are NULL and not 0.00 — the head did not exist, which is a different statement from declaring nothing under it.

A FIGURE IS NOT ALWAYS BESIDE ITS LABEL, and on this form family it is the normal case. These are fillable PDFs: the value a filer types lands where the WIDGET sits, which is not the line the label prints on. Make It Legal's Part B total prints three lines above `TOTAL FOR PART B`; Diana Burgess's candidate total prints on the line `Write 'NIL' if you have NO expenses to declare`. A same-line rule reads both returns as declaring nothing, and the second one PASSED the form's own arithmetic because the parts it did find were 0 and 0 + 0 makes 0.

The form's printed THRESHOLD ($100,000 to file) and CAP are blanked before a line is searched for money. The Public Service Association's NIL return read $100,000 under all three heads, consistent with itself, until they were.
NIL IS A FIGURE and an empty cell is not one. The Commission writes Nil; a blank cell holds nothing to read.
on_fail: The Commission's stated figure loads and `stated_*` stays NULL with the reason. A promoter whose return is not held at all (The Better NZ Trust, 403 twice, ledgered) still carries the Commission's figure, because dropping a figure for want of its document is how 56 donation returns went missing.

title: A notice prohibiting a person from managing companies (Gazette notice: Companies Act 1993 s 382, 383, 385; Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013 banning order)

landmarks: the title 'Notice Prohibiting (a) Person(s) …' together with, or the body alone holding, operative words ('hereby prohibit', 'is (permanently) prohibited', 'must not', 'banning order', 'made an order on', 'hereby revokes') under the Companies Act 1993 or the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013, with the management words ('director or promoter', 'concerned in', 'taking part', 'management of') or a revocation; a body-only match needs a 'To:' field

signals_note: 'Hereby prohibit' alone is not this profile: under section go it also prohibits a doctor's prescribing, a vaccine's import and a fishing method. The Act and the management words are both required.
notes: One template since 2001, mostly section ot (a few go and gn): 'Pursuant to Section 385 of the Companies Act 1993 To: <name>. Of: <address>. Pursuant to section 385(1) …, I, <officer>, Deputy Registrar of Companies, hereby prohibit <name> from being a director or promoter of … for a period of <years and months> as from the date of this notice. Dated at <place> this <n>th (day) of <Month> <year>.' The capture runs fields together ('Smith.Of:', 'ofthis'). Six actions from the operative words: prohibition (the Registrar's, s 385), court order (the Registrar gives notice of a court's order, s 382 and 383, sometimes permanent), banning order (FMC Act; may name two people, two 'To:' fields), variation (a court set aside the Registrar's term; names the notice varied), substitution (a prohibition with a note revoking an earlier notice, named), revocation (revokes a named notice and prohibits nobody; one was revoked 'as published in error' because it named the wrong person, so a revocation's text is never read for a name and the revoked notice's person is not published). The 'Of:' field (or 'Formerly of:') is an address, often a home: private (hard limit 15). An alias in brackets is kept apart from the name. The name is printed twice; both are compared.
applies_to: 537 notices, 2001 to 2026 (535 section ot)
process: Decide the action from the operative words.
Take each 'To:' to 'Of:' as one person; the address to the private schema.
Read the Act and section, the term in months or 'permanently', the start (stated, or the date of the notice), the 'Dated' day, and the notices acted on.
Mark the rows of a notice that a later one revokes, replaces or varies.
gates: Every recognised notice gives a person, is a revocation, or is a catch-log line.
A revocation, substitution or variation names the notice it acts on, and that notice is held.
on_fail: set aside the person or the notice; publish the rest

Read the companies (title, carried-over title, body, or list rows).
Read who appointed, the statute, the date and time per company, the Dated day, the company number where one company prints one.
Read the liquidators from the signature, else the operative sentence.

title: A Registrar-General's list of marriage or civil-union celebrants (Gazette notice)

landmarks: 'celebrant' in the title, or in the first 3,000 characters with a section of the Marriage Act 1955 or the Civil Union Act 2004, or the printed header 'Name of Celebrant Name of Organisation'

signals_note: Recognised by the subject word, never by record shape alone: a bankruptcy list has a celebrant list's shape (the old estate measured 23,139 false positives of 24,875 on shape alone).
notes: Five list shapes: stops ('Surname, Given, Organisation.' and 'Surname, Given.' run together), address (the third field an address: independent celebrants under Marriage Act s 10 and 11 and the Civil Union Act; the address is private), chain ('Surname, Given Surname, Given' with no stops, most lists from 2019: the next surname is the chunk's last word with its particles, or the glue where the space was lost, checked against the list's alphabetical order), marked (the combined annual list from 2016: each name preceded by its letters M and/or CU under the printed key 'CU = Civil Union Celebrant M = Independent Marriage Celebrant'; the letters cut each chunk exactly and are kept as marks; a marked list that prints addresses, 2015, is set aside), table (2000 to 2014, 'Name of Celebrant Name of Organisation': no delimiter between the given names and the organisation, and the organisation glued to the next surname; each chunk between commas is 'given names organisation next surname', or 'given names organisation' with the surname its own chunk. The organisation is cut out by the vocabulary the delimited lists of the same export print, an organisation of two words or more printed in two records or more: the longest that leaves one to five given names before it and a surname after it. A chunk where none fits, or two do, is a catch-log line, and so is the record whose surname it held. The tables are read last, after every other list, so the vocabulary is whole), none (a notice with no list). The action is the notice's own words: appointment, removal, publication ('published for general information' is not an appointment), annual list (says both appointed and published: everyone holding the office for the period), or none when a removal stands beside anything else, or nothing.
applies_to: about 3,000 notices in section go, 2000 to 2026
process: Find the list after the operative sentence and before 'Dated'.
Decide the shape; split records; an address is kept private.
A notice whose action is none gives no rows, only a catch-log line.
Read the printed tables last, cutting each chunk by the organisation vocabulary.
gates: Every recognised notice gives records or a catch-log line.
Every record the reader cannot cut is a catch-log line, never a guess.
A table's person should be named by a delimited list too: the check fails below 70% (measured 79.7%).
on_fail: set aside the record or the notice; publish the rest
